lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: asking for help early and well

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic asking for help early and well task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Given a short fictional workplace scenario where the learner is stuck on a task and unsure whether to keep struggling or ask, the learner practices the ask out loud with a trusted adult playing the supervisor, then revises the ask based on feedback.
safetyNotes: No audio or video recording is made; the adult gives live feedback and the learner writes notes afterward.
The practice scenario is fictional and does not require the learner to discuss any real job or real workplace situation.

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available to role-play the supervisor, the learner instead writes both sides of the conversation as a short script, then reads only their own side aloud once and self-checks it against the same look-fors.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: In the fictional scenario, at what point should the character have asked for help, and how would you recognize that same point in a real task?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Structure of the ask: Ask states what was tried and what specifically is stuck. | Specificity: Ask names the specific step or concept that is the sticking point. | Revision from feedback: Revised ask clearly incorporates the specific feedback given. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner practice a second, harder version: asking for help after having made a mistake that needs to be reported, not just a task they're stuck on, using the same three-part structure adapted for admitting an error.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic asking for help early and well task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

localMaterials.label: paper or notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: asking for help early and well worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Given a short fictional workplace scenario where the learner is stuck on a task and unsure whether to keep struggling or ask, the learner practices the ask out loud with a trusted adult playing the supervisor, then revises the ask based on feedback.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact asking for help early and well decision or action.
Model move 2: Before practicing, write down what makes asking for help at work feel harder than asking a friend.
Model move 3: With your adult playing the supervisor, practice asking for help on the fictional stuck-task scenario, saying what you tried and what you're stuck on.

Model check: Structure of the ask: Ask states what was tried and what specifically is stuck. | Specificity: Ask names the specific step or concept that is the sticking point. | Revision from feedback: Revised ask clearly incorporates the specific feedback given.

resources.title: asking for help early and well action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for asking for help early and well.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: asking for help early and well coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Given a short fictional workplace scenario where the learner is stuck on a task and unsure whether to keep struggling or ask, the learner practices the ask out loud with a trusted adult playing the supervisor, then revises the ask based on feedback.
Coach direction: Before practicing, write down what makes asking for help at work feel harder than asking a friend.
Learner prompt: What is one reason asking a supervisor for help might feel harder than asking a classmate or friend?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: asking for help early and well complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult playing the supervisor, practice asking for help on the fictional stuck-task scenario, saying what you tried and what you're stuck on.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I stated what I had already tried before asking.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I named specifically what I was stuck on, not just 'I don't get it.'
Response 3 (t2-p3): My adult gave specific feedback on the ask.

Equal-access rule: If no adult is available to role-play the supervisor, the learner instead writes both sides of the conversation as a short script, then reads only their own side aloud once and self-checks it against the same look-fors.

resources.title: asking for help early and well minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: In the fictional scenario, at what point should the character have asked for help, and how would you recognize that same point in a real task?

Success checks: Structure of the ask: Ask states what was tried and what specifically is stuck. | Specificity: Ask names the specific step or concept that is the sticking point. | Revision from feedback: Revised ask clearly incorporates the specific feedback given.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: asking for help early and well supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional asking for help early and well condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Structure of the ask: Ask states what was tried and what specifically is stuck. | Specificity: Ask names the specific step or concept that is the sticking point. | Revision from feedback: Revised ask clearly incorporates the specific feedback given..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u03-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
